description: Just a team with a big dream
summary: Outpost Dial is a browser game that helps children ages 7–12 explore what it takes to run a Mars outpost. Over ten Martian days, players assign three astronauts to jobs that generate power, recycle water, build radiation shielding, and collect science. Real, archived NASA DONKI records supply solar storms, while limited forecasts challenge players to prepare and bring exposed crew to shelter. Cadet and Commander modes offer different rescue challenges. After each mission, players can see the dates and space-weather events behind their run. The game connects real NASA data to choices children can make, showing why a crew must balance resources, forecasts, and safety when conditions change.
details:
Outpost Dial is a Mars outpost game for ages 7–12, built as a static site with JavaScript ES modules and Vite. A Node script fetches NASA DONKI flare, solar-particle and CME records in 60-day batches, links related events, identifies CME arrivals at Mars and writes a JSON archive. The browser loads this snapshot; it needs no backend or live NASA API.

A seeded run builder turns a ten-day historical window into daily storms and CME forecasts. Game rules live in a pure step() function, separate from the interface. It calculates power, water, shielding, science and crew radiation from the player’s astronaut assignments, then returns the next state and mission log. UI modules render an SVG outpost, controls, gauges and rescue flow. localStorage saves progress after each sol.

Vitest and jsdom test the rules and screen flows. A balance script simulates 1,000 missions per mode to check difficulty and whether using forecasts improves outcomes. GitHub Actions tests and builds the site on Node 22; Cloudflare serves the static files.
